title: Bregman asks for it, and the Yacht Club broadcasts
summary: Publisher Jack Bregman wanted the tune as publishers fought to plug songs during the band's coast-to-coast broadcasts from the Yacht Club on 52nd Street.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: He say yeah, yes, that's all right. Let's use it. So Fats got in and put in his two cents, and changed -- he maybe changed a few chords here and there, and maybe, you know, and we started using it for a theme song, and people started coming in, and saying hey Fats, what is that? He'd say aw, that's some little new thing we did there. And they'd say it is? And one publisher said give it to me! Give it to me! Back -- Bregman.

Yeah, and the other guys came in there because at that time they were having a fight about tunes. You know, different guys -- you know, the big three, Robbins, so and so and so and so and so, you remember? The publishers?
What was the fight about? I mean what --

Well, I mean who can -- you had a tune you wanted to get plugged, another guy would -- you know, they would say, you know. And we were broadcasting what, twice a week, three times a week, coast to coast from the -- from 52nd Street at the Yacht Club.
